correctness.rationale: The Fernandes--Paulista dihedral extension theorem, checked in the primary preprint, says every partial cycle isometry restricts a dihedral symmetry, uniquely for domain rank at least 3; nonunique rank-two antipodal restrictions require correction. If alpha=g|D self-inverse at rank>=3, D invariant under g and g^2 fixes >=3 points, forcing g^2=id since a nontrivial dihedral permutation fixes at most two. Each group involution contributes (1+z)^f(1+z^2)^t for invariant domains, according to fixed points and transpositions. Odd n: identity + n reflections each (f,t)=(1,(n-1)/2); even n: n/2 vertex-axis reflections (2,(n-2)/2), n/2 edge-axis reflections plus halfturn (0,n/2). The group sum overcounts rank0 by n (odd) or n+1 (even), rank1 by n, and rank2 by 0 (odd) or n (even); subtract precisely those terms. Independently enumerated all self-inverse metric partial bijections from scratch for n=4..8, giving complete predicted vectors (1,4,12,8,6), (1,5,20,20,10,6), (1,6,30,32,36,12,8), (1,7,42,56,56,42,14,8), (1,8,56,80,124,80,64,16,10). Finite counts corroborate the universal group-theoretic argument.
